6 تخامص عَنْهُ (tropical:) He shrank, or drew away, from it; (A, K; *) i. e., from anything of which he disliked the nearness. (A.) You say, مَسَسْتُهُ بِيَدِى وَهْىَ بَارِدَةٌ فَتَخَامَصَ مِنْ بَرْدِ يَدِى (tropical:) [I touched him with my hand, it being cold, and he shrank from the coldness of my hand]. (A, TA.) ―
-b2- تَخَامَصْ لِفُلَانٍ عَنْ حَقِّهِ (tropical:) [Relinquish thou, i. e.,] give thou, to such a one, his right, or due. (A, K. *) ―
-b3- تخامص اللَّيْلُ (tropical:) [The night retreated;] the darkness of the night became thin a little before daybreak. (A, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
